 Print Vijayawada : Educational institutions in at least eight districts of Andhra Pradesh will remain closed on Tuesday, as a precautionary measure in view of the heavy rainfall and strong winds forecast under the influence of Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu. The districts where holidays have been announced include NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, Prakasam, Nellore and Markapuram. The respective district administrations have taken this decision, keeping student safety in mind amid the possibility of heavy to extremely heavy rainfall as the cyclone approaches the Andhra Pradesh coast. In the NTR district, Collector Dr G. Lakshmisha announced a holiday for all government and private schools, junior colleges, degree colleges and Anganwadi centres. He directed all educational institutions to comply with the order and warned of stringent action against those violating the instructions. Similarly, Nellore and Prakasam district administrations have declared holidays for government, private and aided schools, Anganwadi centres and junior colleges on Tuesday. Palnadu district has also announced the closure of educational institutions in view of the approaching cyclone. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast that Murasu will cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, near Ongole, around midnight on Monday or in the early hours of Tuesday. The severe cyclonic storm is expected to bring sustained wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph during landfall. The weather department has warned of heavy to very heavy rainfall at several places and extremely heavy rainfall at isolated locations across the state. District administrations have been taking precautionary measures, including activating control rooms and keeping emergency response teams on standby. Students and parents have been advised to follow announcements from their respective district administrations and avoid unnecessary travel during adverse weather conditions. The holiday declarations are district-specific, and there is no statewide closure order.
